own_solution.law: Apply 1/f = 1/u + 1/v successively. The first lens forms an image at v1 = (12×36)/(36−12) = 18 cm. This supplies a real object 45−18 = 27 cm in front of the second lens, giving v2 = (9×27)/(27−9) = 13.5 cm behind it. Increasing the lens separation by 14 cm gives u2 = 59−18 = 41 cm and v2 = (9×41)/(41−9) = 11.53125 cm.
assumptions: Use the standard thin-lens, paraxial geometrical-optics model.
The lamp illuminates the object without changing its position or the lenses' optical properties.
A displacement in an earlier experiment does not change the explicitly stated present lens separation.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T5121 and T1356 replace the explicit 14 cm displacement in their corresponding displacement variants with an unspecified 'small distance', violating the requirement that variants preserve the same number and unit.

notes: The base optical problem is well-posed under the permitted standard thin-lens idealization. T81BC and TEA01 describe a displacement from the stated 45 cm separation before the requested image location is determined, yielding a final separation of 59 cm. TBA57 and T5121 concern an earlier experiment and leave the present configuration unchanged. Object height enters the paraxial ray and magnification relations but cancels when determining the axial image position, so both height sentences are C. Lamp displacement changes illumination but has no path to the requested image position in this model. Both height variants consistently specify 3.5 cm. The invalid verdict concerns the displacement variants' failure to preserve their numerical specification.
